title: Ananias of Damascus (Acts 9:10–19)
hookLine: he's afraid of Saul, goes anyway, and calls him brother

cards: Saul on the road to Damascus, the light, the fall, the voice: that's the half of this story painters love. The second half belongs to a man who appears for only a few verses: Ananias, a disciple living in Damascus.
He isn't an apostle, he leaves no letters, and he has heard all about Saul, the man who has been dragging believers off to prison. And one day the Lord tells Ananias to go and find him.

teach.b: The instructions are oddly precise. In the Douay-Rheims: "Arise, and go into the street that is called Strait," and seek, in the house of Judas, one named Saul of Tarsus. He's praying, and he's blind.

teach.h: ANANIAS ARGUES: I KNOW THIS MAN.
teach.b: And Ananias does something very human: he argues. Lord, I've heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints in Jerusalem, and he's here with authority to arrest everyone who calls on your name.
That's not a lack of faith. It's memory. He knows exactly who Saul is.
The answer doesn't take the danger away.
Go thy way, the Lord says, "for this man is to me a vessel of election," to carry my name before the Gentiles. So Ananias goes.
Picture the walk down that street, the knock, the blind man who once came to arrest people like him. And the first two words out of Ananias's mouth, in the Douay-Rheims: "Brother Saul." Not enemy.
He lays his hands on him, and immediately something like scales falls from Saul's eyes.
He sees, he gets up, he is baptized, and he eats. The future apostle Paul is welcomed into the Church by a disciple who appears for only a few verses.
Tradition places the street called Straight on the long main street of old Damascus. And Ananias is honored as a saint: a frightened man who knocked anyway.

how: Catholics honor Ananias of Damascus as a saint, and they hear this passage at Mass in the Easter season and on the feast of the Conversion of Saint Paul on January 25.

games.q: you're Ananias. the Lord tells you to go to the man who came to Damascus to arrest believers like you. what do you do?
o: say you're afraid, and go anyway.
send someone else in your place.
games.why: he says exactly what he's heard about Saul, then goes, lays hands on him, and calls him brother Saul.

practice: Think of a person you avoid, not someone dangerous, just someone hard: the one who hurt you, the one who intimidates you, the conversation you keep postponing.
Notice what your body does when you picture them; Ananias felt that too, and said so out loud.
Then imagine your first two words if you went, something like brother, or sister, or friend, and if you pray, tell God plainly what you're afraid of, the way Ananias did.

wordCard.voice: Brother. The first word Ananias said to Saul, the man he feared, instead of enemy or persecutor. Today's word.
